title: Why Homebrew paths differ on Apple Silicon and Intel Macs
summary: Homebrew installs programs in /opt/homebrew on Apple Silicon Macs (M1 and later) and in /usr/local on Intel Macs. Guides and paths must match your chip, or the shell will not find the program.

prerequisites: Homebrew installed (only needed for the second step)

steps.explain: Check which chip your Mac has. arm64 means Apple Silicon (M1 and later). x86_64 means an Intel Mac.
steps.expect: arm64 on Apple Silicon Macs, x86_64 on Intel Macs.

steps.explain: Print the folder where Homebrew is installed. /opt/homebrew means the Apple Silicon Homebrew, /usr/local means the Intel Homebrew. Use the folder this command prints, not the one from an older guide.
steps.expect: /opt/homebrew on Apple Silicon, /usr/local on Intel. A 'command not found' message means Homebrew is not installed or not on PATH.

verify.expect: Prints /opt/homebrew (Apple Silicon) or /usr/local (Intel), matching the chip from uname -m.

warnings: A terminal opened with Rosetta ('Open using Rosetta') reports x86_64 from uname -m even on an Apple Silicon Mac. Trust the folder from brew --prefix when you need to know which Homebrew is in use.
Do not copy /usr/local/bin paths onto an Apple Silicon Mac, or /opt/homebrew paths onto an Intel Mac. The program is not found at the wrong folder.
